in-anentome-helena.title: Assassin Snail
in-anentome-helena.sci: Anentome helena (also sold as Clea helena)
in-anentome-helena.summary: A striped predatory freshwater snail kept to hunt bladder, ramshorn and Malaysian trumpet snails.
rows: About ¾–1 in in stores; can grow larger when well fed
Stable community tanks; groups of 5–6 need enough pest snails or supplemental protein food
Predatory toward other snails; generally peaceful with community fish and larger shrimp
Carnivore. Live snails, carrion, plus protein foods (bloodworm, flakes) and mineral support for the shell
About 75–80°F (Aquarium Care Basics); Aquarium Co-Op cites 70–80°F
About 7.0–8.0; harder water supports shell health
Moderate / easy if water is stable and food is available
notes: Plant-safe. Cover intakes so snails are not trapped.
Will eat desirable snails if hungry or if pest snails run out.

in-nerite-snail.title: Nerite Snail
in-nerite-snail.sci: Neritidae (trade includes Vittina waigiensis / red racer, zebra, horned, olive, etc.)
in-nerite-snail.summary: Popular algae-eating snails that clean glass and hardscape without overrunning a freshwater tank.
rows: About dime-to-quarter size depending on type (roughly 0.5–1.5 in)
Works in 10 gal+ community tanks; nanos OK if not overstocked. Tight lid required
Peaceful; avoid loaches, crayfish, goldfish and cichlids that may eat them
Algae browser / scavenger. Soft film, green and brown algae, diatoms, leftover food; supplement if the tank is too clean
Alkaline preferred (~7.5); harder water and calcium help shells
Coastal and brackish-associated waters; freshwater aquarium strains are widely farmed/collected for the trade
notes: White hard egg capsules appear in freshwater but rarely hatch without brackish rearing.
Place snails upright — many struggle to flip themselves over.
